md_description: This workflow models airborne particulate collection from urban locations such as parks, industrial zones, and residential areas, followed by microbial genome sequencing and computational analysis of airborne community composition and dynamics. It links physical sampling of air particles, sequencing of recovered microbial DNA, and downstream derivation of taxonomic and abundance profiles used to study urban microbial exposure and potential human health relevance. Environmental metadata including time of day, temperature, humidity, wind speed, and proximity to green spaces or pollution sources are captured as contextual descriptors for each sampling event.

ambient_air_at_urban_location.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic identity/origin and contextual properties of the sampled ambient air at the urban site before any collection or measurement. I focused on location category and environmental context that define the air source in this workflow, while excluding sampling operation details, sampler hardware, DNA preparation, sequencing, file-level data, and downstream computed results. I also avoided duplicating any identifier-like fields that could overlap with later nodes, especially sample or experiment IDs, since those are not specified here and should appear once at the root entity if needed. The fields are shaped by the experiment description’s emphasis on urban site type, time of day, weather, and proximity to green spaces or pollution sources.

md_schema.descr: Categorical descriptor of the ambient air sampling site before collection; use to indicate the urban setting in which the air was present at the time of sampling. Allowed values are exhaustive for this workflow: park, industrial_zone, residential_area, roadside, other_urban_site. Do not use for sampler placement or later analysis grouping.

Local date and time when the ambient air was considered sampled at the site, recorded at the moment of field collection start or the reference time used for environmental annotation. Format example: 2026-08-18T07:30:00. Use local site time, not UTC.

Categorical time-of-day context for the ambient air at sampling, recorded from the field observation or derived from sampling_datetime_local. Use to capture broad diurnal context relevant to airborne microbial dynamics. Allowed values: dawn, morning, midday, afternoon, evening, night.

Air temperature in degrees Celsius at the sampling site at the time of ambient air collection or site annotation. Typical urban range: -20 to 50 Celsius. Record as measured in the field near the sampler inlet, not from downstream processing.

Relative humidity of ambient air at the sampling site at the time of collection, expressed as percent. Typical range: 0 to 100. Measure in the field near the sampler inlet and do not confuse with laboratory humidity.

Wind speed at the urban sampling site during ambient air collection, in meters per second. Typical range: 0 to 30 m/s for urban field sampling. Record from the field weather observation nearest the collection time.

Categorical assessment of how near the sampled air location was to green space at the time of collection, used as site context for airborne microbial exposure. Allowed values: adjacent, nearby, distant, not_applicable. Use based on the local site context, not on later statistical grouping.

Categorical assessment of how near the sampled air location was to an obvious pollution source such as heavy traffic, industrial emissions, or smoke at the time of sampling. Allowed values: adjacent, nearby, distant, not_present. Use as a contextual descriptor of the ambient air source environment.

air_filter_collection.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only how high-volume air sampling was performed and the key operational parameters of the collection step, plus the agent hardware description required for operation nodes. I excluded ambient site context fields such as temperature, humidity, wind, and urban location because those belong to the upstream Entity, and I excluded filter identity/output file fields because the collected filter entity will own those properties. I also avoided any downstream sequencing or DNA preparation details. No previously generated fields were present in this turn, so there were no direct naming conflicts to resolve.

md_schema.descr: Duration of the high-volume air collection run in minutes, measured from sampler start to sampler stop at the urban site. Typical range for this workflow: 5 to 1440 minutes. Record the actual elapsed collection time for the filter/substrate loading event.

Volumetric airflow rate through the high-volume sampler during collection, in liters per minute. Typical urban field range depends on instrument model, often 100 to 1000 L/min. Record the set or monitored operating rate during the collection process.

Total volume of ambient air drawn through the sampler during the collection run, expressed in cubic meters. Typical range: about 1 to 2000 m3 depending on duration and flow rate. This is measured or calculated from the active collection parameters for the completed sampling event.

Type of collection medium used to trap airborne particles during high-volume sampling. Use the material actually loaded into the sampler for this process. Typical examples include filter, quartz_filter, PTFE_filter, glass_fiber_filter, or other_substrate.
Manufacturer of the high-volume air sampler used for the collection step. Record the hardware vendor name for the active instrument performing air draw and particle capture.
Model name or number of the high-volume air sampler used for collection. Use the instrument model as configured during sampling; example format: HVS-1000 or equivalent vendor model string.

Serial number or unique hardware identifier of the high-volume air sampler used during the collection event. Use the manufacturer-assigned identifier format exactly as printed on the instrument label or service record.

Observed or specified particle capture efficiency of the collection step, expressed as percent. Typical range: 0 to 100. Record the effective capture performance for this sampling run if available from the instrument or validated protocol.

collected_air_particle_filter.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the recovered particle-loaded filter itself: what substrate it is, how much material it contains, its physical condition, and chain-of-custody style origin from the sampling event. I excluded collection process parameters such as duration, airflow, sampler hardware, and efficiency because those belong to the upstream Process node. I also excluded downstream DNA extraction, sequencing, or file-level attributes because those belong later in the DAG. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, and I avoided introducing sample or experiment identifiers that would duplicate root-level entity metadata elsewhere in the workflow.

md_schema.descr: Material or construction type of the recovered collection substrate containing trapped airborne particles and microbial biomass. Examples include PTFE, quartz_fiber, glass_fiber, cellulose, or other filter material. Record the intrinsic substrate composition of the entity after collection.

Diameter of the recovered filter substrate in millimeters, measured on the collected entity after sampling or from the substrate specification. Typical values for air sampling filters are 25 to 110 mm depending on the instrument.

Total ambient air volume represented by the trapped material on this filter, in cubic meters, as carried forward from the completed sampling event. Typical range: about 1 to 2000 m3. Use only if tracked on the filter entity as a property of the collected material rather than the sampler process.

Estimated total microbial biomass or nucleic-acid-equivalent load on the collected filter, expressed in nanograms. Typical range depends on site and duration, often 0 to 10000 ng. Record as an intrinsic property of the collected entity if measured before extraction.

Physical condition of the recovered filter immediately after collection and before downstream processing. Allowed values: intact, partially_damaged, torn, folded, visibly_soiled, wet, dry. Use the state of the entity as received for preparation.

Storage temperature of the collected filter entity after retrieval from the sampler and before downstream preparation, in degrees Celsius. Typical values include 4, -20, or -80 depending on preservation workflow. Record the storage condition associated with the entity, not the ambient field temperature.

Elapsed time in hours between end of collection and start of downstream sample preparation. Typical range: 0 to 168 hours. Use as a property of the recovered filter entity only if tracked as part of specimen handling history.

Human-readable label for the origin site or sampling event associated with this recovered filter, such as a park, industrial zone, or residential area label. Use a descriptive origin tag, not a separate sample ID or experiment ID.

sample_preparation.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the preparation workflow and protocol parameters used to convert the collected filter into sequencing-ready DNA, plus a key quality indicator of the prepared material and the operator/software agent if relevant. I excluded the upstream filter’s physical properties and storage history because those belong to the collected entity, and I excluded the downstream sequencing-ready DNA intrinsic properties beyond preparation output quality because the DNA entity will own its own descriptors. I also avoided repeating any sample or site identifiers. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, so I only avoided semantically upstream/downstream territory rather than explicit name collisions.

md_schema.descr: Name of the DNA extraction or sample preparation protocol applied to the collected particulate filter. Use the protocol as executed for this workflow, for example bead-beating extraction, silica-column extraction, or other validated protocol name.

Commercial kit or reagent system used during sample preparation to recover microbial DNA from the collected air particulate sample. Provide the kit name and vendor if available, for example a microbial DNA extraction kit or equivalent reagent set.
Physical or chemical method used to lyse microbial cells during preparation of the filter material. Allowed values: bead_beating, enzymatic_lysis, chemical_lysis, heat_lysis, combined_method, none.

Mass of particulate material or filter material processed in the preparation step, in milligrams, when the workflow specifies a subsample rather than the full filter. Typical range: 0 to 1000 mg. Record the amount actually entered into the preparation protocol.
Final DNA elution volume from the preparation step, in microliters. Typical range: 10 to 500 µL. Record the volume used to recover sequencing-ready microbial DNA from the extraction matrix.

Total nucleic acid or microbial DNA yield obtained at the end of sample preparation, expressed in nanograms. Typical range depends on biomass and method, often 0 to 10000 ng. Use as an output-quality indicator for the preparation process.

Measured absorbance ratio A260/A280 for the prepared DNA fraction at the end of sample preparation. Typical DNA quality range is about 1.7 to 2.1. Record the post-preparation quality check value if measured.
Person or role responsible for carrying out the sample preparation step. Use a human-readable name or role string, for example researcher, technician, or lab_member.

sequencing_ready_dna.reasoning: I corrected the sequencing_ready_dna Entity schema by removing the colliding field dna_purity_ratio_260_280, which had already been generated for an earlier DAG step. I kept only non-duplicative intrinsic DNA properties that remain within this node’s territory: concentration, total amount, fragment size, 260/230 purity, storage condition, and sequencing readiness flag. I excluded protocol, reagent, and sequencing run details because those belong upstream or downstream, not to this Entity node.

md_schema.descr: Measured concentration of the prepared microbial DNA, expressed in nanograms per microliter, at the point the material is deemed sequencing-ready. Typical range for environmental samples: 0 to 1000 ng/µL. Record the post-preparation concentration used to determine whether the material is suitable for sequencing.

Total amount of sequencing-ready DNA available in the prepared extract, expressed in nanograms. Typical range: 0 to 10000 ng. Use this as the intrinsic mass of the prepared entity after purification and before sequencing library construction.

Approximate dominant fragment size of the prepared DNA, in base pairs, as measured after sample preparation and before sequencing. Typical environmental DNA ranges may span 100 to >20000 bp depending on extraction and shearing. Record the main size used to judge sequencing readiness.

Absorbance ratio A260/A230 for the prepared DNA at the sequencing-ready stage, reflecting contamination by salts or organic compounds. Typical acceptable range is approximately 1.8 to 2.2. Record the value measured before sequencing library construction or direct sequencing.

Current storage condition of the sequencing-ready DNA entity before sequencing, indicating how the material is held to preserve integrity. Allowed values: fresh, refrigerated, frozen, thawed, lyophilized.

Boolean indicator that the prepared DNA passed internal QC and is suitable for sequencing library construction or direct sequencing at the time of annotation. Use true only if the entity met the workflow’s acceptance criteria.

dna_sequencing_capture.reasoning: This node is a Capture, so I included only the sequencing session and instrument configuration used to read the prepared DNA, plus capture-specific run metrics and the instrument hardware identity required for operation nodes. I excluded DNA-intrinsic fields such as concentration, fragment size, and purity because those belong to the upstream sequencing-ready DNA entity, and I excluded raw file properties because those belong to the downstream Signal node. To fix the collision noted previously, I did not reuse dna_purity_ratio_260_280 or any equivalent purity field here. I also avoided downstream analysis parameters and output interpretations.

md_schema.descr: Sequencing technology platform used for the capture session, describing the instrument class performing the readout of prepared microbial DNA. Allowed values: short_read, long_read, hybrid, other_platform. Use the platform active during this capture step, not the downstream analysis software.

Instrument run identifier assigned to this sequencing session, used to link all raw reads generated from the prepared DNA. Example format: run_YYYYMMDD_001 or vendor-specific run ID string. Use the capture-session identifier, not a sample ID.

Configured or nominal read length in base pairs for this sequencing capture session. Typical short-read values are 50 to 300 bp; long-read platforms may be substantially longer. Record the intended read length used by the instrument during capture.
Boolean indicator of whether this sequencing capture was performed in paired-end mode. Set true for paired-end short-read runs and false for single-end or equivalent capture modes.

Target number of reads or read pairs intended for this capture session, measured as an instrument planning parameter before or during the run. Typical range depends on project scale, from 1000 to >1000000000. Use the target depth for this sequencing event.
Manufacturer of the sequencing instrument used for the capture step. Record the hardware vendor name for the active sequencer reading the DNA.
Model name or number of the sequencing instrument used for the capture step. Use the exact instrument model string when available, for example NovaSeq 6000 or equivalent vendor model.
Serial number or unique hardware identifier of the sequencing instrument used in this capture session. Use the manufacturer-assigned serial or asset identifier for the instrument.

raw_sequencing_reads.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I included only raw data artefact properties: file format, size, read count, technical dimensions, quality metrics, and storage location. I excluded sequencing instrument settings because those belong to the upstream Capture node, and I excluded cleaned-read parameters and biological interpretation because those belong to downstream Process and Derivative nodes. I also avoided any reuse of upstream DNA quality or capture identifiers, and I checked that the previously generated dna_purity_ratio_260_280 collision is not repeated here. The fields are tailored to FASTQ-like raw reads produced for each urban sampling location.

md_schema.descr: Technical file format of the raw sequencing read artifact produced by the capture step. Use the on-disk encoding actually stored for the data object, for example FASTQ, gzipped_FASTQ, BAM, or other raw-read container. Record the file format at the point the signal is archived.

Total file size of the raw sequencing read artifact in bytes, measured for the stored data object. Typical range depends on depth and platform, from 1000000 to >100000000000 bytes. Record the archived signal size for downstream transfer and storage planning.

Number of sequencing reads contained in the raw signal file set, counted after basecalling and before any preprocessing. Typical range: 1000 to >1000000000 reads depending on sequencing depth. Use the total raw read count represented by the artifact.

Total number of called nucleotide bases represented in the raw reads, measured across the complete raw sequencing artifact. Typical range scales with read depth and read length, from 1000000 to >1000000000000 bases. Record as the raw signal content size.

Mean per-base quality score across the raw sequencing reads, summarized for the file set as stored. Typical raw-read values vary by platform and run, often in the range 20 to 40. Use the technical quality metric of the raw signal, not a biological QC result.

Overall GC percentage of the raw sequencing reads, expressed as percent. Typical microbial metagenomic raw-read values may span roughly 20 to 80 percent depending on community composition. Record the signal-level base composition for the archived raw data.

File path, object store URI, or accession pointing to the archived raw sequencing read data. Example formats include local file paths, s3 URIs, or repository accessions. Record the location of the signal artifact itself.
Boolean indicator of whether the raw sequencing file is stored in compressed form. Set true for compressed FASTQ or equivalent archived signals and false otherwise.

read_preprocessing.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the computational preprocessing workflow: the software used, its version and repository, the operations performed, key trimming/filtering parameters, and a run-level output quality indicator. I excluded raw-read file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded clean-read file properties because those belong to the downstream Signal node. I also avoided duplicating any upstream instrument settings or downstream taxonomic interpretation. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, so I focused on process semantics and software provenance required for reproducibility.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software used for read preprocessing, such as the adapter trimming and filtering tool applied to raw sequencing reads. Record the exact program name used in this workflow step.
Version string of the read preprocessing software used at this step. Example format: v0.23 or 0.23.4. Record the exact version for reproducibility of trimming and filtering behavior.
Repository, package source, or code location for the read preprocessing software used in this step. Examples include GitHub URL, Bioconda package name, or vendor repository reference.
Boolean indicator that adapter trimming was performed on the raw sequencing reads during preprocessing. Set true if adapters were removed and false if no adapter trimming was applied.

Minimum per-base Phred quality score threshold used to filter or trim reads during preprocessing. Typical values are 10 to 35 depending on the stringency of the workflow. Record the threshold applied to the raw reads before downstream analysis.
Minimum read length in base pairs retained after preprocessing. Reads shorter than this threshold are discarded or clipped away. Typical values are 20 to 100 bp for short-read cleanup workflows.

Maximum allowed proportion of ambiguous bases (N) in a read, expressed as percent, used as a filtering criterion during preprocessing. Typical values are 0 to 20 percent depending on software settings.

Percentage of raw reads that passed preprocessing and were retained as clean reads, used as a run-level quality indicator for this process. Typical range: 0 to 100. Measure after trimming and filtering are complete.

clean_reads.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I included only technical properties of the processed read artifact itself: output file format, size, retained read count, length distribution, quality metrics, and storage location. I excluded preprocessing software, adapter trimming, and filtering thresholds because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded taxonomic or functional interpretation because that belongs downstream. I also avoided repeating any previously generated field names or equivalent meanings from other nodes. The schema is designed to let downstream users inspect and reuse the cleaned read set before profiling.

md_schema.descr: Technical file format of the cleaned sequencing reads after preprocessing. Use the stored on-disk encoding actually used for the cleaned signal artifact, for example FASTQ, gzipped_FASTQ, or other archive format.

Total file size of the cleaned read artifact in bytes, measured for the archived post-preprocessing data object. Typical range depends on retained depth and compression, from 1000000 to >100000000000 bytes.

Number of reads retained after preprocessing, counted in the cleaned read artifact before downstream profiling. Typical range: 1000 to >1000000000 reads depending on sequencing depth and filtering stringency.
Total number of nucleotide bases present in the cleaned reads after trimming and filtering, measured across the archived post-preprocessing signal. Typical range scales with read count and length.
Mean read length in base pairs after preprocessing, calculated from the cleaned read artifact. Typical range depends on platform and trimming stringency, often 20 to 300 bp for short-read data.
Mean per-base quality score across the cleaned reads, summarized for the post-preprocessing signal. Typical values are often 25 to 40, depending on platform and filtering settings.
GC percentage of the cleaned sequencing reads, expressed as percent. Typical metagenomic values may span roughly 20 to 80 percent depending on community composition and trimming behavior.
File path, object store URI, or accession pointing to the cleaned read data artifact. Example formats include local paths, s3 URIs, or repository accessions.

community_profiling.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the computational profiling method and its configuration: the profiling software identity and provenance, the database or reference used, key inference parameters, and a summary-quality indicator of the profiling run. I excluded clean-read file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded the derived taxonomic table itself because that belongs to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided environmental metadata and capture settings, which are out of scope here. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, so I focused on process-level reproducibility and the assumptions that shape taxonomic inference.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software used for microbial community profiling from cleaned sequencing reads. Record the exact program name applied in this workflow step, for example a taxonomic classifier or abundance estimator.
Version string of the community profiling software used at this step. Example format: v2.1 or 2.1.0. Record the exact version to ensure reproducibility of classification behavior.
Repository, package source, or code location for the profiling software used in this step. Examples include GitHub URL, Bioconda package name, or vendor repository reference.
Name of the taxonomic or genomic reference database used during community profiling. Examples include a specific microbial genome database, curated marker database, or custom reference set.
Version or release identifier of the reference database used for profiling. Example format: release_2024_01 or v1.2. Record the exact database version used for inference.

Minimum confidence threshold required for taxonomic assignment during community profiling. Typical values range from 0 to 1 for probabilistic classifiers or 0 to 100 for percent-based scores depending on the software.
Minimum relative abundance threshold used to report taxa in the profiling output, expressed as percent. Typical values are 0 to 1 percent, depending on reporting stringency.

Percentage of cleaned reads assigned to one or more taxa by the profiling pipeline, used as a run-level quality indicator for this process. Typical range: 0 to 100. Measure after classification is complete.

taxonomic_abundance_table.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only computed-result properties of the abundance table itself: table schema, dimensions, taxa resolution, abundance units, normalization, and result-level quality indicators. I excluded the profiling software and reference database because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded raw or cleaned read properties because those belong to upstream Signal nodes. I also avoided downstream comparative-statistics fields because those belong to the later analysis derivative. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, so I focused on the minimal metadata needed to interpret and reuse the derived abundance matrix.

md_schema.descr: File or serialization format of the derived taxonomic abundance table. Use the actual stored format for the result artifact, for example TSV, CSV, parquet, or JSON. Record the format of the computed table itself, not the input reads.

Number of rows in the derived abundance table, typically corresponding to taxa, features, or sample-by-feature records depending on the table layout. Record the final output dimension after profiling.
Number of columns in the derived abundance table, including taxa labels, sample identifiers, and abundance fields as applicable. Record the final matrix or table width after profiling.

Lowest taxonomic rank represented in the derived abundance table. Allowed values: domain, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species, strain, mixed_rank. Use the resolution actually reported by the profiling result.

Unit used to express abundance values in the derived table. Allowed values: relative_abundance_percent, read_count, normalized_count, log_abundance, other. Use the exact unit or scale reported by the derivative.

Method used to normalize counts or abundances in the derived table, if any. Examples include none, total_sum_scaling, rarefaction, centered_log_ratio, or other documented normalization. Record the computation applied to produce the final abundance values.

Minimum abundance threshold used to retain taxa in the final derived table, expressed as percent if the table reports relative abundance. Typical values are 0 to 1 percent. Record the reporting cutoff for the computed result.

Boolean indicator that the derived abundance table passed internal consistency checks, such as expected dimensions, nonnegative values, and valid taxonomic labels. Set true when the computed result is considered usable for downstream comparative analysis.

comparative_analysis.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the statistical/computational analysis setup used to compare community profiles across urban site categories, plus the agent software provenance and high-level output quality indicators of the analysis run. I excluded the abundance table contents because those belong to the upstream Derivative node, and I excluded the final comparative conclusions because those belong to the downstream results Derivative node. I also avoided reusing any previously generated software/database fields unless they were semantically specific to this analysis step. The fields are tailored to reproducible urban comparison of microbial profiles across parks, industrial zones, and residential areas.

md_schema.descr: Name of the statistical software or analysis package used for the comparative analysis step. Record the exact tool used to compare microbial community profiles across urban site categories.
Version string of the comparative analysis software used at this step. Example format: v4.4 or 4.4.1. Record the exact version to ensure reproducibility of the statistical results.
Repository, package source, or code location for the analysis software used in this step. Examples include an R package name, GitHub URL, or vendor repository reference.

Name of the statistical method or model used to compare microbial communities across urban environments. Examples include PERMANOVA, differential abundance testing, ordination-based comparison, or mixed-effects modeling.

Primary grouping variable used for the comparison of microbial profiles in this analysis step. Typical values in this workflow are urban_site_category, proximity_to_pollution_source_category, or time_of_day_category.
Method used to correct for multiple statistical tests in the comparative analysis, if applicable. Examples include none, BH, Bonferroni, or FDR.

P-value threshold used to determine statistical significance in the comparative analysis. Typical values are 0.05 or 0.01. Record the cutoff applied when interpreting differences across urban environments.

Minimum effect size or analogous cutoff used to report meaningful differences in community profiles, if applicable. Use the metric in the units defined by the chosen statistical method; if no threshold was applied, record 0.

Boolean indicator that the comparative analysis completed successfully and passed basic checks such as model convergence, valid input dimensions, and nonempty outputs. Set true only if the analysis result is considered usable for reporting.

urban_microbiome_results.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only computed-result properties of the comparative output: result format, dimensions, what comparisons were made, key summary statistics, and result-level significance/quality indicators. I excluded analysis software and statistical settings because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded the abundance table because that is an input derivative rather than this result. I also avoided repeating any upstream grouping-variable or significance-threshold fields when they would merely restate the process, instead focusing on the properties of the derived result object itself. The schema is meant to support reuse and interpretation of the final urban comparison output.

md_schema.descr: Stored format of the derived comparative results artifact. Use the actual serialization or document form of the result object, for example TSV, CSV, JSON, HTML, or report. Record the format of the computed result itself.
Number of rows or result records in the derived comparative output, such as taxa, comparisons, or test statistics entries. Record the final size of the result object after comparative analysis.
Number of columns or result fields in the derived comparative output, including identifiers, test statistics, and summary measures. Record the final width of the result table or object.

Scope of the comparisons represented in the derived result object. Allowed values: between_sites, between_habitats, time_of_day, pollution_proximity, combined_model, other. Use the scope actually summarized by the result artifact.

Name of the main summary statistic reported in the derived result, such as fold_change, p_value, q_value, effect_size, ordination_axis, or distance_metric. Record the primary numeric summary returned by the computation.

Number of taxa, features, or comparisons meeting the analysis significance criterion in the derived result. Typical values are 0 to many hundreds depending on table size. Record the count of items highlighted by the comparison.

Significance cutoff associated with the derived comparative result, expressed as a p-value or equivalent threshold used for reporting. Typical values are 0.05 or 0.01. Record the threshold as it pertains to the final result artifact.

Boolean indicator that the derived comparative results passed output validation, such as nonempty comparisons, finite statistics, and expected result dimensions. Set true only if the result object is usable for interpretation and downstream reporting.
